title: Sebastian and the Choir
premise: Ulyana Thornbury keeps the ledgers of the Vesper Choir, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled echoes, borrowed luck, doors to countries erased from maps. When the crown declares a hunt for anyone carrying the gift of 'unmaking,' Ulyana's own quiet talent for rewriting what is written marks them as prey. To survive, they must follow a ledger entry their dead mother left behind and find the last door out of Vellichor, a country that officially no longer exists, while deciding whether loyalty to the Choir that sheltered them matters more than the truth it has been selling. In the end, Ulyana opens the door—but chooses to stay long enough to burn the ledgers, freeing every debt-bound soul in the guild before walking through into the winter.
about_author: Freya Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paperwork of defunct institutions before turning to fiction. They write about people trapped by systems, and the small acts of forgery that set them free.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. We meet them cataloguing impossible inventory for the Vesper Choir: a jar of last year's summer, a key that opens yesterday. Their gift—making written things true—is hidden even from themselves, disguised as clerical accuracy. Emotional beat: cozy routine shadowed by the first royal proclamation nailed to the guild door.

chapters.title: Proclamation of the Hunt
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The crown offers silver for anyone with the gift; neighbors begin counting each other's shadows. The Choir's mistress, Odile Vesper, orders all members to pass as ordinary. Ulyana notices their own handwriting on an old deed has quietly made a ruin habitable—and realizes what they are. Beat: dread mixed with vertiginous self-discovery.

chapters.title: What Odile Keeps in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with a flashback interlude. Sent to fetch inventory, Ulyana finds the cellar full of confiscated gifts from past hunts—proof the Choir has survived by betraying its own. Odile catches them and offers protection at a price: total obedience. Beat: loyalty begins to curdle into complicity.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Among the ledgers they find their mother's handwriting: an entry for a door out of Vellichor, annexed and erased twenty years ago. The door can only be opened by someone whose name was written there before the erasure. Beat: grief transformed into purpose; inheritance becomes a map.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Tobias, a fellow scribe and Ulyana's closest friend, POV. Tobias, starving and terrified, reports a stranger with the gift to the crown—then discovers the stranger was innocent. He realizes the Choir knew and let him do it. Beat: guilt; the hunt turns neighbor against neighbor, and Tobias begins keeping his own secret ledger.

chapters.title: Borrowed Luck
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Using bottled luck from the inventory, Ulyana slips past a checkpoint to reach the archive where Vellichor's records were sealed. A young soldier with the gift herself lets them go, asking only to be remembered. Beat: the price of survival made flesh—someone always pays for your luck.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Odile reveals she knows about the door and offers to open the way out—if Ulyana rewrites the guild's founding charter, making her authority literally true and permanent. Ulyana must choose between escape and complicity. Beat: the trap of gratitude; loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Tobias POVs. Snow seals the passes; the hunt reaches the city. Tobias, unable to live with his guilt, brings Ulyana the evidence of Odile's betrayals instead of reporting them. Beat: forgiveness offered cautiously; two liars choosing truth together as the world whitens.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Vellichor
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax. Ulyana signs the charter as Odile demands—but writes a second clause beneath it, unbinding every debt the guild holds. Odile's power dissolves mid-confrontation as the cellar's confiscated gifts fly free. Ulyana opens their mother's door with their true, pre-erasure name. Beat: triumph purchased with everything familiar.

chapters.title: What Is Written Remains
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue-like. On the far side of the door lies Vellichor as it was—not restored, but remembered into being. Ulyana sends word back to Tobias and the freed debtors, then begins writing a new first ledger: a record of everyone the old one erased. Beat: bittersweet resolution; inheritance reclaimed as authorship.
